messages:
Alex W.: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selection tweak (prefer fast-f32 kernels for small heads) we're seeing higher GPU memory fragmentation and a drop in prefix cache hit-rate on p99 workloads. OOMs spiked on two prod nodes.
Sara L.: Ugh. Any quick repro? numbers?
Alex W.: Repro on canary: sequence lengths ~80, but many short prefixes (~10–30). Hit-rate dropped from ~72% -> 55% on prefix-cache, GPU mem free dropped by ~200MB on average, fragmentation metric (free_chunks_variance) up 3x.
Pranav: Did the kernel change increase per-request temporary allocations? Could be more per-token scratch for the fast path.
Maria: We saw that fast-f32 path allocates a small transient buffer per head when using the fused-attn fallback. Might blow slab packing.
Evan: oom-alert-bot: [ALERT] node rwd-ix-07 triggered OOM-kill at 2026-03-17T11:22:10Z. Backtraces attached.
Alex W.: Attached logs in the thread:
```
2026-03-17T11:21:50Z serve: req_id=fa3a prefix_key="user:chat:123:pre_42"
alloc: GPU slab insert size=48KB -> slab 4/16 used
free_chunks_variance=0.42 -> 1.45
kv_hit=false
2026-03-17T11:22:10Z oom: kill process serving-runtime pid=4021
```
Sara L.: Key thought: our cache key normalization currently includes session metadata timestamp. Small changes in session fields -> cache churn. That plus fragmentation -> fewer reusable blocks.
Pranav: Hypothesis: kernel selection changed execution timing causing slightly different allocation ordering -> slab fragmentation worsened. Combined with increased key cardinality (session ts) -> effective working set larger.
Maria: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) canonicalize prefix keys to strip ephemeral session fields; 2) increase GPU slab size for small allocations (coalesce slots); 3) tune TTL ramp to prefer longer-lived entries for prefixes with >X hits.
Evan: For 2), increasing slab size might reduce packing efficiency for mixed-size allocations. We should simulate: run a micro-benchmark with mixed prefix sizes and the new kernel path.
Alex W.: I ran a micro-bench already: attaching results — two configs: slab-4k / slab-64k. Hit-rate / OOMs: slab-4k: hit 55%, 2 OOMs in 30m. slab-64k: hit 68%, 0 OOMs. But median allocation latency went up 8%.
Sara L.: Tradeoff seems acceptable for prod tier with high p99 requirements. Could set slab-64k on dedicated nodes and keep slab-4k on low-cost pools.
Pranav: Also worth adding an LRU hot-cohort: if a prefix is seen >3x in 1m, bump TTL to 5m automatically (warmup strategy). That reduces churn and improves coalescing.
Maria: Implementation note: bumping TTL should update both CPU and GPU caches atomically. We had a race before where GPU TTL was longer than CPU and caused double-counting.
Evan: Another idea: prefill warmup for canaries — when a model variant is selected, prefetch top-K prefixes from recent traffic to populate KV with proper slab placement. Might be costly but helps tail.
Alex W.: TL;DR action items: @Sara to canonicalize keys patch + unit tests, @Pranav to prototype TTL bump policy in staging, @Maria to run slab-size microbench across instance types, @Evan to schedule prefill experiment on a small canary ring.
Sara L.: I'll open PR with key normalization today, adding a flag to enable/disable. small patch: trim session_id and ephemeral flags from prefix hash.
Pranav: I'll add TTL-bump in cache controller. quick pseudocode: 
```
if hits(prefix, window=60s) >= 3:
  set_ttl(prefix, max(curr_ttl, 300))  # seconds
```
We'll gate with feature flag and metrics.
Maria: Running microbench matrix now (kernels x slab sizes x batching heuristics). Expect results in ~6 hours.
Evan: For rollout, propose: canary ring with slab-64k + key-normalize + TTL-bump enabled. Monitor kv_hit, free_chunks_variance, and p99 latency. If kv_hit > 65% and no OOMs after 2h, roll to dedicated.
Alex W.: +1. Also add metric for "cache-coalesce_score" (fraction of allocations that reused existing slab block) so we can see packing behavior.
oom-alert-bot: [INFO] Created incident rwd-2026-03-17-oom-evict for tracking.
Sara L.: Noted. I'll link PRs and experiments to the incident.
Pranav: One more: check batching heuristic interplay — larger batches might increase temporary KV usage (longer KV lifetimes during request). If TTL-bump interacts with batch window, watch for delayed evictions.
Maria: Good call. I'll include batch-window variations.
Alex W.: Thanks team. If we can get the canary config up by EOD we'll reduce risk for tomorrow's peak.
Sara L.: On it. :rocket:
